# pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server sendmail notification endpoint: notifications PBS hands, as mail, to the mail transport agent of its host — Postfix on a standard installation — which delivers them, or relays them as it is configured to. A notification reaches an endpoint only through a matcher: route notifications to this one with a `pbs_notification_matcher` whose `target` names it.

**The built-in `mail-to-root`** mails `root@pam` at the email address PBS has for it, and is where the built-in `default-matcher` sends notifications. It cannot be created or deleted, only changed: manage it by importing it, and destroying the resource resets it to its built-in settings.

~> **PBS refuses to delete an endpoint a matcher targets.** When a change of `name` replaces an endpoint that a `pbs_notification_matcher` targets, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on the endpoint, so that the matcher moves to the new endpoint before the old one goes.

Endpoint and matcher names share one namespace. Managing notification endpoints needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`, reading them `Sys.Audit on /system/notifications`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Mail handed to the host's mail transport agent, which delivers or relays it
# as it is configured to. A notification reaches the endpoint only through a
# matcher that targets it, such as in the pbs_notification_matcher example.
resource "pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail" "admins" {
  name         = "backup-admins"
  mailto       = ["backup-admins@example.com"]
  mailto_user  = ["root@pam"]
  from_address = "pbs@example.com"
  author       = "Backup server"

  # A test mail on every apply that creates or changes the endpoint.
  send_test_on_apply = true
}

# The built-in mail-to-root, which default-matcher targets, imported to mail
# the backup admins as well. Destroying this resource does not delete it: PBS
# resets it to its built-in settings.
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail.mail_to_root
  id = "mail-to-root"
}

resource "pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail" "mail_to_root" {
  name        = "mail-to-root"
  comment     = "Send mails to root@pam's email address"
  mailto_user = ["root@pam"]
  mailto      = ["backup-admins@example.com"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`; `mail-to-root` for the built-in endpoint, which must be imported. Matchers name it in `target`. Changing it replaces the endpoint.

### Optional

- `author` (String) Sender name of the mails, which appear from `<author> <from_address>`; `Proxmox Backup Server - <host name>` when left out.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `disable` (Boolean) Whether the endpoint is disabled: matchers that target it send nothing through it. Defaults to `false`.
- `from_address` (String) Sender address of the mails; when left out, the email sender address in the node's settings, or `root` at the host when that is not set either.
- `mailto` (Set of String) Mail addresses to send notifications to. At least one of `mailto` and `mailto_user` is required.
- `mailto_user` (Set of String) Users, such as `root@pam`, to send notifications to, at the email address PBS has for each; a user without one gets nothing.
- `send_test_on_apply` (Boolean) Have PBS send a test notification through the endpoint after every apply that creates or changes it, unless it is disabled, so that a wrong setting fails the apply instead of going unnoticed until a real notification is lost. Defaults to `false`. It exists only in Terraform: turning it on changes nothing in PBS and sends nothing by itself, and every test delivers a real message. A successful test means that the host's mail transport agent accepted the mail, not that it delivered it. A failed test fails the apply. When the test after a create fails, the provider deletes the endpoint again, so the next apply creates and tests it again — should that delete fail too, the endpoint is kept and marked tainted; when the test after an update fails, the endpoint keeps the change, and the next apply tests again only if the endpoint changes again. Sending a test needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.
- `origin` (String) Where the endpoint comes from: `user-created`; `builtin` for `mail-to-root` with its built-in settings; `modified-builtin` once it is changed.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail.mail_to_root
  identity = {
    name = "mail-to-root"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, such as `mail-to-root`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail.mail_to_root
  id = "mail-to-root"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Sendmail endpoints are imported by name, the built-in mail-to-root included.
terraform import pbs_notification_endpoint_sendmail.mail_to_root mail-to-root
```
